gsd-plan-checker.md.reason: #3771 splits the remediation channel into a binding payload and a non-binding example. The growth is the split itself, carried where the model reads it: a `required_property` line on each of the 18 dimension examples (an example missing a required field is exactly the drift that produced this bug — a schema the examples contradict teaches the examples), the two new schema fields with their BINDING/NON-BINDING legend, the normative paragraph stating that a smaller mechanism reaching the same property addresses the issue in full and that a hint contradicting a visible constraint must be declared rather than emitted, the blocker/warning rendering reworked so "must fix" names the property and displays the hint as an example, and the matching clauses in `<adversarial_stance>` and `<success_criteria>` — a rule present in the body but absent from the checklist is a rule the agent is never told to apply. No prose was moved into an eagerly @-imported reference to shrink the measured file; total loaded context grew by exactly this diff, and the file remains inside its LARGE tier cap.

gsd-ui-checker.md.reason: #3771 applies the same separation to the UI-spec checker, which the Agent Brief names as ordering literal application even more directly than the plan-checker. The growth is a `required_property` line on each of the six dimension issue examples plus one paragraph stating that the hint is an example, that a smaller mechanism reaching the same property resolves the issue in full, and that a hint contradicting a locked user answer must be declared rather than emitted. It reuses the plan-checker's wording deliberately: one contract stated twice in the two files that produce these issues, rather than a shared reference neither checker loads. Second pass (review): the `## ISSUES FOUND` structured return and the BLOCKED verdict line still ordered "exact fix required" and rendered `Fix: {exact fix required}`. That rendering is the surface the researcher actually reads, so marking only the dimension examples left the prescription shipped; both now name the property, its evidence, and a non-binding example.

plan-phase.md.reason: #3771 gives the plan-phase revision loop the conflict path it lacked. The growth is two blocks: the revision prompt gains the binding/advisory statement and the order to re-check locked decisions, capability guidance and existing plan constraints before editing; and the loop gains REVISION_CONFLICT handling ahead of the iteration counter and the stall check. The second block has to sit in the workflow rather than in `revision-loop.md`, because it is this file that owns `iteration_count`, `prev_issue_count` and the stall/escalation ladder — a conflict is not resolvable by re-running the same loop, so routing it without spending an iteration is orchestrator state, not shared prose. The shared halves of the contract did go to `gsd-core/references/` (planner-revision.md, revision-loop.md), which is why only the state-owning part landed here. Second pass (review): the conflict branch became executable rather than declarative — it reads workflow.plan_review_convergence, records the conflict in the phase REVIEWS.md that convergence already consumes, and excludes routing back into a run convergence itself started, which would be a cycle. It also drops the "accept as-is" option, which was an early exit from a still-failing blocker. Third pass (round-2 review): the convergence hand-off was replaced outright. "Unless this run was invoked by convergence" is not a question the orchestrator can answer at runtime, so plan-phase no longer invokes convergence at all — it records the conflict when a phase REVIEWS.md exists, resolves it with the user in place, names itself the owner that strikes the row resolved, and bounds recurrence on a repeated required_property so declining to spend an iteration cannot make the path unbounded.

ui-phase.md.reason: #3771 gives the UI-spec revision loop the same conflict path, for the same reason the plan-phase one needed it in the workflow: this file owns `revision_count`, so declining to spend an iteration on an unresolvable conflict is state only it can act on. The growth is the binding/advisory statement plus the constraint re-check in the researcher's revision prompt, and one bullet routing REVISION_CONFLICT to the user with its alternatives before the checker is re-spawned. Second pass (review): the increment moved off the pre-dispatch path onto the return path — a counter spent before dispatch cannot be withheld when REVISION_CONFLICT comes back, so the rule was unreachable prose — and the blocker-bypass option was removed for the same reason as plan-phase. Third pass (round-2 review): same recurrence bound, for the same reason.

diagnose-issues.md.reason: #3771 marks the gap-closure hint non-binding. The debugger's `suggested_fix` fed the gap plan through the same fused channel — a remediation string with no statement of what actually binds. The growth is three lines renaming it to `fix_hint` (reconciling the last drifted field name in the same pass) and stating that the binding payload is `root_cause`, so a gap plan that removes the root cause by a smaller or different mechanism has closed the gap in full.

plan-review-convergence.md.reason: #3771 gives the convergence loop the receiving end of the conflict route. Review found the first pass declarative: plan-phase said "hand the conflict to that loop" and nothing in this file could take it. The growth is three clauses on an existing seam rather than a new mechanism — the converged exit refuses to fire while REVIEWS.md carries an unresolved `## Plan-Revision Conflicts` entry, the replan step is told that re-running the planner against an unchanged conflict cannot resolve it and must instead adopt an alternative, override the named constraint or amend it, and the success checklist gains the matching condition so a gate present in the body is not absent from the checklist. REVIEWS.md was chosen because this loop and its reviewers already consume it; inventing a hand-off channel would have cost far more than these lines. Second pass (round-2 review): the gate had been written after `gsd_run state planned-phase` and the success banner, which would have written and announced convergence over an unresolved conflict. OPEN_CONFLICTS is now read from REVIEWS.md with awk and is part of the converged condition itself, evaluated before any write.

verify-work.md.reason: #3771 round-2 review found this flow missed. verify-work's gap-plan revision loop hands `<revision_context>` to gsd-planner, so it inherits the whole revised contract whether or not it states it — a planner reading planner-revision.md can return REVISION_CONFLICT here, and before this change nothing in the loop could receive it. The growth is the two blocks every other revision-bearing flow now carries: the binding/advisory statement plus the constraint re-check in the planner's instructions, and the conflict branch that declines to spend an iteration, offers only resolving options, and bounds recurrence on a repeated required_property. No new mechanism — the same wording as plan-phase and quick, in the file that owns this loop's iteration_count.
